newsitem.title: FINLAND: Imatran Voima says may seek listing in spring '98.
newsitem.headline: Imatran Voima says may seek listing in spring '98.

text.p: Finnish state-controlled energy group Imatran Voima Oy's (IVO) incoming CEO said on Thursday IVO would not seek a bourse listing in 1997, but that this time next year could be appropriate.

Earlier, IVO had indicated that a listing might be in the pipeline this year, but chief financial officer Heikki Marttinen, who will become chairman and CEO on April 1, told a news conference on the release of the group's 1996 results that certain factors had delayed that timetable.
"It would hardly make sense to try to seek a listing in November-December, but next year instead," Marttinen said.
"Perhaps the most appropriate point in time would be when the (1997) profit and loss account is ready," he said.
Asked whether he was referring to a listing application in March-April 1998, Marttinen said. "Yes, let's go for that."
"This is the view on our side, and we have talked with the ministry of trade and industry about when it would be our turn and they seem to think along the same lines," he added.
The Finnish state directly owns 96 percent of IVO and the remaining four percent through the National Pension Institution (KELA). -- Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
